comment: Read from src/Ledger.cpp at commit 71e0bcb, the last commit whose plugin.json carries the installed 2.0.30. Three places where the README and the code disagree. The README says a block becomes independent once both its inputs are connected; Ledger.cpp:272 tests only the second input, so patching the first input alone leaves the block cascading. The README says an unconnected first input is normalled to NOT the first input of the block above; Ledger.cpp:264 normals it to that block's first flip-flop, which is not the same thing and is not brought out to any jack. The README describes the second input as normalled to the same operation's result from the block above; Ledger.cpp:265 normals it to the previous block's second flip-flop. Two internal results never reach a jack: the first flip-flop, used only for normalling, and the NOT of the second input. The XOR in a cascading block is (first gate OR previous XOR) AND NOT the new AND (Ledger.cpp:76), which is not an exclusive-or of two independent terms. The panel-theme submenu is plugin-wide and cosmetic, so it has no line.
